title: Record a 29-shear one-scale zero-swap word for helper-462.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Constructive witness, one finite census, and a rank lower bound. No new κ and no selected-frontier change. The selected value stays `781451/250000000`.

For the pinned helper-462 matcher, the alphabet of axis swaps, single-coordinate rational scales and rational shears contains a zero-swap word with exactly one scale and **29 shears**. The scale is the last letter, on row 0, with coefficient `-16`. Shear denominators are `1, 2, 4, 8, 16`. The merged elimination in #6954 has **53** shears on the same matrix and the same scale. Twenty-nine is strictly shorter.

Twenty-nine is the minimum inside one finite elimination family: column order `0..7`, pivot row equal to the column index, each non-unit pivot repaired either by one shear from a strictly lower nonzero row or by one 4-shear balanced scale, then the usual clearing. The census discards a partial branch only when its shears already number at least as many as a completed word. The same minimum is 29 for every scale row except row 2, where it is 30. This is a census of that family. It is not a census of every rational shear word.

Every zero-swap one-scale word has at least **8** shears. Moving the scale to the end, by the identity `B D A = D (D^{-1} B D) A`, preserves the shear count, and `rank(D^{-1} S - I) = 8` for every scale row. A product of `k` elementary shears has rank distance at most `k` from `I`. The integers 9 through 28 stay open. A failed search outside the family would not close them.

No supplier admission, no P2 ordinary bill, and no integer-coefficient claim. The integer obstruction remains the theorem of #6954. This word uses the denominator 16.

## Task and overlap

Base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`, priority revision 8. The verifier reads `certificates/selected-result.json`; `current-priorities.md` on this base still quotes the older selected value from #5599.

Task card: `supplier-boundary-audit`, scope **refined**. The question is open question 1 of merged #6954 and of discussion comment [19507194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19507194): the minimal shear count of a zero-swap word that uses exactly one scale. The requested first step was to keep one scale of coefficient `-16` and replace one balanced-scale block by a shorter shear identity. This word replaces every balanced-scale block and every signed exchange.

Nearest work, and why this is distinct:

- Merged #6954 records a one-scale word of length 53 and proves that one scale is necessary. This package starts from that word and shortens the shear count.
- Merged #6947 records a swap-free 7-scale 27-shear route. It uses seven scales.
- Merged #6950 prices that 7-scale word under the P2 ordinary bill. No tariff is recomputed here.
- Open #7012 records a 25-shear word with eleven scales. That is the at-least-two-scale question, and 25 is not a one-scale length.

A column-order probe that returned no word pivoted only on rows that were already nonzero and demanded a second nonzero before changing a non-unit entry. Columns 0 and 1 of `D^{-1} S` are single entries equal to 2, so that filter has no move. The 29-shear word imports row 5 into row 0, whose column-0 entry is 0. The empty return is that filter, not a lower bound.

Package: `research/helper462-one-scale-fewer-shears`.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B research/helper462-one-scale-fewer-shears/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/helper462-one-scale-fewer-shears/verify.py
python3 -O -B research/helper462-one-scale-fewer-shears/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/helper462-one-scale-fewer-shears
```

Proof controls use an explicit failure function, so they stay active under `-O`. Expected token: `PASS_HELPER462_ONE_SCALE_FEWER_SHEARS`.

Checked here: the published 5-swap word and the new word both multiply to the pinned matcher, by row operations and by elementary matrices; the predecessor breakdown on the same matrix is 15 exchange + 28 balanced + 4 clear + 6 back = 53; the canonical repair is 6 normalizations + 10 clears + 13 back-substitutions = 29; the repair-family minimum is 29; moving the scale preserves the count and the product; `rank(D^{-1} S - I) = 8`; dropping any letter, replacing the scale by `-8` or `+16`, or adding 1 to the first shear misses `S`.

No Lean, Docker, or selected cold replay was run.

## Credit

The matcher and the five-swap elimination are from `research/bit-completed-backend-api` (Chris R / Clear1nsight, PR #4957), using the helper-462 witness of ai-nanachi #4760/#4814. The 53-shear one-scale word and the determinant identity are PR #6954. The 7-scale 27-shear schedule is PR #6947. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Is there a zero-swap word with exactly one scale of coefficient `-16` and fewer than 29 shears? The family census uses column order `0..7`. The rank bound is 8, so 9 through 28 are open. Rational coefficients make the set of words of length at most 28 infinite.
2. Can the rank lower bound of 8 be raised under the same hypotheses? Subadditivity of `rank(W - I)` meets 8 on this matrix, so a stronger bound needs a different invariant.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The column-order probe that returned no word was a different pivot filter from the 29-shear elimination. Recording that filter next to the word that does import a zero pivot row kept the empty return from being read as a lower bound.
